summary: Explicitly stop serving a shared publication without resetting its revision, silently falling back, or deleting source and artifacts.
agentOutcome: An agent receives an explicit withdrawn state instead of obsolete shared context. It can inspect the state and request a new reviewed proposal; local Core/Observer and unrelated publications remain usable.

api.withdraw: POST /api/v1/projects/{project}/publications/{publication}/withdrawal with exactly expected_revision. Administrator only; expected revision is a nonnegative integer below signed BIGINT maximum. No filesystem, source-currentness, quality gate or preparation job is required to revoke a selection.
api.startupBoundary: This operation does not bypass Server startup configuration validation. A running Server can withdraw after source disappearance; a cold process still requires valid configured catalog paths. The missing-source cold-start test explicitly removes unavailable catalog entries from private runtime configuration while preserving durable publication history. No configuration repair or route fallback is automatic.
api.receipt: Return {replayed,receipt}. Receipt schema shin.publication-withdrawal-receipt.v1 contains id, project_id, publication_id, expected_revision, revision, previous_proposal_id, previous_preparation_id, withdrawn_by and created_at. Revision advances by one. While the receipt remains retained, exact retries for a consumed revision return it even after republishing; it is historical acknowledgement, not current head state. Explicitly retired older withdrawal retries conflict with the preserved monotonic head rather than executing again.
api.head: Read-only head returns state empty, active or withdrawn. Only never-published is empty/revision zero. Withdrawn has its persisted positive revision and null source/artifact selection. State does not claim source currentness.
api.retrieval: New search/Brief/Pack admission against withdrawn selection fails HTTP 410 publication-withdrawn before source/catalog/artifact access. No fallback to the private route, cached generation or previous selection. A request admitted before withdrawal can finish against its explicitly reported old revision; withdrawal does not cancel in-flight readers.
api.base: A subsequent proposal may use a known withdrawn revision with an empty base and a typed withdrawal identity. Historical accepted bases retain their existing artifact rules. Unknown or future base revisions remain conflicts. Accepting a new proposal uses the normal source, quality and head-CAS checks.

storage.ledger: Migration 013 preserves 001..012 and adds immutable publication_withdrawals. Active heads remain active-selection rows; withdrawal deletes only that pointer. Latest accepted/withdrawn transitions reconstruct the monotonic logical head in one SQL observation, detecting missing/inconsistent pointers rather than resetting to zero.
storage.identity: Withdrawal references its exact previous accepted resolution. UNIQUE(previous_proposal_id) permits at most one withdrawal per accepted proposal, so history is structurally bounded by already admitted proposals. Withdrawal remains available when proposal admission is full.
storage.proposalBase: A new nullable base_withdrawal_id on proposals is permitted only for a positive withdrawn base with null base_preparation_id. Its composite foreign key binds project, publication and exact base revision. Existing initial/accepted bases are preserved.
storage.audit: The existing typed audit publication_proposal_id points to the previous accepted proposal for publication.withdrawn. Its unique withdrawal identity is reconstructible from that immutable association; no overloaded free-text identifier or new audit field is required.
storage.transaction: Project authorization, publication-writers transaction fence, exact revision check, head deletion, immutable withdrawal and audit commit together. Audit failure rolls everything back. No preparation row lock is acquired after the audit fence.
storage.retention: Removing a shared head releases only that head's artifact pin. Other active routes, heads, unresolved proposals and admitted native readers still protect their artifacts. Withdrawal performs no artifact deletion.

acceptance: Active -> withdrawn -> newly accepted transitions are monotonic and survive restart without Git.
All three retrieval operations refuse a withdrawn warm selection, including after source disappearance.
Exact retry, concurrent retries and an uncertain/lost reply produce one withdrawal and one audit event.
Concurrent accept and withdrawal consuming the same revision have one winner; stale actions never overwrite the winner.
Forbidden roles, invalid inputs, future revisions and empty/already-withdrawn transitions do not mutate state.
Withdrawal remains possible at proposal capacity; history is bounded by the accepted-proposal uniqueness constraint.
Audit-trigger failure rolls back both pointer and ledger; explicit artifact retention respects remaining pins and readers.
Schema upgrade preserves existing publications, all ordered checksums and runtime role restrictions.
nonGoals: No automatic invalidation or source mutation
Withdrawal never prunes history; explicit pruning is owned by shin-publication-history-v1
No remote source export or semantic merge
productClosure: Later release closure must evaluate complete agent workflows, time to verified useful context, excess file reads, explicit refusal handling and recovery, not just isolated throughput. A source-backed whole-product gap review is still planned.
